review_notes: I read the whole file. Its only definitions are the local instances and one theorem, and the theorem is a case-split wrapper that I did not treat as a duplicate. I grepped the CorvajaZannier directory and found the same hand-built `Algebra K[X] L` local instance, plus the matching scalar-tower instance, in about 18 files. I checked Mathlib for `Algebra.compHom`, which gives the same algebra map. I did not open every copy, and I did not check that swapping in `Algebra.compHom` compiles. This is a weak match for the rubric. The main cost is repetition inside this library, not a competing public concept, and a definitional-unfolding or instance-diamond issue could remain.

findings.problem: This local instance builds `Algebra K[X] L` by hand with `RingHom.toAlgebra` on a composed ring hom. Mathlib already has `Algebra.compHom`, which is documented as composing an `Algebra` with a `RingHom`. It sets `algebraMap := (algebraMap R A).comp f`, which is exactly this composite for `f = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)`. The same construction is repeated under different names in about 18 files of this library, for example `principalDivisorPolynomialAlgebra` and `residuePolynomialAlgebra`. The matching `IsScalarTower K[X] (RatFunc K) L` proof is repeated as well. So there are many independent local `Algebra K[X] L` structures. Each file also needs its own scalar-tower proof and torsion-free, finiteness and integrality instances.
findings.proposed_change: Define the `Algebra K[X] L` structure once in a shared upstream module as `Algebra.compHom L (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K))`. Add the scalar-tower instance there once, and import or open it in each file. Delete the per-file `...PolynomialAlgebra` copies, including this one. If a local instance must stay, define it as `Algebra.compHom L (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K))` rather than by hand.
findings.benefit: Readers see the standard Mathlib construction and its `compHom_algebraMap_eq` lemmas instead of about 18 near-identical hand-rolled instances. All files would then share a single `Algebra K[X] L` structure, so the instances cannot drift apart or diverge between files.
